content:
Olivia: Quick sync — I've pulled together customer asks and internal proposals for the Optimize toolkit. Need to shape MVP scope for the next cycle: batching suggestions, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations, and eval-triggered alerts. Thoughts?
Sam: thanks. can we prioritize deliverables that unblock customer pilots first? batching heuristics + a simple rec API seem highest impact.
Maria: +1. quant recs are tricky — we should ship a guidance table (model x workload -> recommended q/precision) before automated conversion flows. easiest win: 4-bit profiles for our top 3 verified models.
Anita: customers keep asking for: 1) per-route batch sizing advice, 2) TTL-based prefix cache suggestions, 3) regression alerts tied to eval suites. they'd accept manual recommendations initially.
Ryan: for prioritization, I'll run an econ signal to estimate token-cost savings if customers apply batch / cache recs. quick back-of-envelope shows 12-18% cost reduction on conversational workloads with decent batching.
Chris: devex request — we should ship an SDK sample and a one-page runbook with any MVP. even short code examples reduce friction a lot.
Olivia: proposal: MVP includes (A) Recs API that returns batching + cache + quant suggestions given workload meta, (B) Eval-Alerting v1 that triggers on eval regressions and maps to suggested mitigations, (C) docs + SDK examples. Defer automated quant conversion and auto-enforcement to v2.
Sam: scoping question — Recs API shape? should just be read-only suggestions (JSON) or an ops endpoint that can apply configs? I vote read-only for safety.
Maria: agree read-only. draft suggestion schema:
```
{
  "workload_type": "chat|completion|embedding",
  "recommended_batch_size": 8,
  "cache_policy": "prefix_ttl:30s,kv_cache:enabled",
  "quant_recommendation": "q4_0 for gpt-3.4, q4_1 for llama-70b",
  "confidence": 0.84,
  "notes": "based on latency/cost profile for 16-64 token responses"
}
```
Anita: customer asks we should capture now: include a field `expected_savings_estimate` and a human-readable rationale for compliance/security-sensitive teams.
Olivia: good call — add `expected_savings` and `compliance_notes`. Also launch criteria suggestion: 1) Recs API responds for 3 verified models, 2) Eval-Alerting fires correctly on two baseline eval suites, 3) docs + SDK examples published, 4) 2 pilot customers onboarded and confirm >5% cost improvement or fewer latency SLO breaches.
Chris: timeline? if eng can commit a small spike this week, we can aim for a canary rollout in 4 weeks and GA in ~12.
Sam: ok I'll prototype API and simple heuristics this week. assigning: Sam -> prototype API + canary infra, Maria -> quant guidance table + perf validation, Ryan -> savings model + dashboards, Chris -> docs + sample, Anita -> recruit 2 pilot customers and consolidate asks.
Olivia: tagging next steps in notion: https://redwood.company/s/optimize-playbook (internal). Please update your tasks by EOD. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled: canary branch will be created once Sam opens PR (ci/tests will run).
Maria: one more note — eval alerts should include an option to suppress noisy regressions (thresholds + rolling windows). default: three consecutive eval runs >2% regression triggers alert.
Anita: customer feedback loop — we'll ask pilots for 3 canonical prompts and expected quality thresholds so evals map to product impact.
Sam: will post API proto and sample response later today.
Olivia: thanks team — I'll consolidate decisions and send an updated scope doc by tomorrow morning. :eyes:
